title: Evaluate normalized DNS domain policy
prompt: Implement solve(payload), a purely lexical DNS policy evaluator with no DNS lookups. rules contains {"domain":string,"subdomains":boolean,"action":"allow"|"deny"}; queries contains strings. Normalize domains by ASCII lowercasing and removing exactly one final dot. A valid normalized domain is 1..253 characters; labels are 1..63 ASCII letters/digits/hyphens, with an alphanumeric first and last character. Empty labels, whitespace, wildcard syntax and Unicode are invalid. A rule matches its exact domain and, only when subdomains=true, names ending in "."+domain. Most labels in the matching rule wins; deny wins a tie. No match means deny. Return {"decisions":[ "allow"|"deny"|"invalid", ...]} in query order. An invalid rule domain or action returns {"error":"invalid_rule"} before evaluating queries. Numeric labels are permitted as lexical DNS labels. Any numeric inputs are finite; inputs have the documented shapes; unspecified validation is out of scope. Do not mutate payload or any nested value. Numeric absolute tolerance 0, relative tolerance 0; strings, booleans, errors and collection shapes must match exactly.
bad_solution:
def solve(payload):
    return {"decisions": ["allow" if any(q.endswith(r["domain"]) and r["action"] == "allow" for r in payload["rules"]) else "deny" for q in payload["queries"]]}
